title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 Astra to Pro, Enterprise
content:
Update: A day later, GPT-6 Astra is rolling out to Business and Pro customers on the $100/month or $200/month plan. This follows other new model releases before Plus customers on the $20/month plan gain access.
It’s been just over a year since OpenAI released the first GPT-5 models for ChatGPT. Now it’s time for GPT-6 Astra to upgrade ChatGPT and Codex capabilities. Details below.
GPT-6 Astra details
OpenAI has officially detailed its new model, GPT-6 Astra, which it calls “the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.”
Here’s more from the official announcement today:
GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work. Astra saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score, having already helped solve long-standing open problems in mathematics. Astra also saturates ARC-AGI-3 with a 99.9% score and ExploitBench with a 100% score. It also sets a new frontier on computer and browser use, handling the most demanding professional work with unmatched speed, accuracy, and judgment.
OpenAI goes further on how GPT-6 improves computer use, which allows ChatGPT to use your Mac or other desktop, including in the background while you work:
GPT‑6 Astra pairs advances in computer use with targeted training for professional environments, to help tackle complex work tasks. It combines the intelligence required for complex problems with the ability to carry out multistep workflows and produce polished documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
Additionally, GPT-6 Astra is “the best model for software engineering to date,” OpenAI says.
In terms of Codex specifically, here’s something new about GPT-6:
With Astra, we’re introducing a new way for Codex to preserve and retrieve context when the context window fills. Historically, models have used compaction to summarize work during long sessions, such as when debugging complex issues or tackling large refactors. Each compaction can leave out details about why a fix failed or how a component behaves. In Codex, Astra can keep notes across context windows, preserving accumulated details without repeatedly compressing them into a single summary. Earlier context windows remain searchable, so Astra can find requirements or test results from previous messages and tool outputs—even if that information wasn’t captured in its notes. You can enable this experimental feature in your Codex, and it will become the default for Astra in the coming weeks.
OpenAI calls GPT-6 Astra a “significant jump in cyber capabilities,” adding that it “meets the Critical threshold in cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework.”
For that reason, the model is rolling out slowly to users.
“GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS,” OpenAI says.
“Astra usage is included within the existing subscription allowances—users and businesses will also be able to purchase credits for additional usage. Users on the Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans will also get access to GPT‑6 Astra Pro. Enterprise administrators can enable Astra for their workspace; access is off by default at launch.”
The road to GPT-6 Astra
GPT-5 launched August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and several reasoning models as ChatGPT’s default. Its defining feature was automatic routing: ChatGPT could answer quickly or invoke deeper reasoning depending on the request. OpenAI also claimed fewer factual errors than GPT-4o.
Apple adopted the model with iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests passed through Apple Intelligence, including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and visual intelligence, switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5.
GPT-5.1 promised warmer, more natural answers in November. December’s “code red” GPT-5.2 accelerated professional work in response to Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant targeted ChatGPT’s “cringe” tone, followed two days later by GPT-5.4 Thinking with a million-token context window and built-in computer use.
OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for more autonomous work, GPT-5.5 Instant, and July’s GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models.
From the Codex Mac app to a new ChatGPT
The software around those models transformed too. OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app in February as a hub for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling work.
In July, Codex effectively became the new ChatGPT desktop app, combining Chat, Work, and Codex while the previous native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.
For me, Codex has changed how I work with ChatGPT the most. I’m able to offload a lot more work that doesn’t require critical thinking and even build tools on my Mac that I couldn’t put together otherwise.
GPT-6 availability
OpenAI says its new GPT-6 models will only be available to its cyber security-focused Daybreak program members to start. This echoes a similar release cadence with the previous model release, GPT-5.6.
Here’s what OpenAI says about availability, specifically:
GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS.
You can learn much more about OpenAI’s latest frontier model here.

report.summary: OpenAI begins rolling out GPT-6 Astra to Pro and Business subscribers, touting major gains in coding, computer use, and cybersecurity.
report.background: The announcement comes just over a year after GPT-5 replaced GPT-4o, and after a rapid series including GPT-5.1 through GPT-5.6. OpenAI has emphasized automatic routing, warmer tone, larger context windows, and autonomous computer use, partly in response to pressure from rivals like Gemini. During that time, OpenAI integrated Codex into the ChatGPT desktop app, shifting from a separate Mac coding assistant to a unified hub for chat, work, and multi-agent coding. Astra follows GPT-5.6’s cautious release cadence, with cybersecurity-focused Daybreak members getting early access because the model meets 'Critical' thresholds under OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework. Rolling out slowly to organizations and tiers reflects growing concerns over dual-use capabilities, while keeping subscription allowances mostly intact.
key_points: Availability is tiered and cautious. OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra starts with a limited set of organizations and Daybreak cybersecurity members, then rolls out over coming days to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, API, and AWS. The update notes Pro and Business users on $100 or $200 plans are getting access before $20 Plus subscribers. Enterprise admins must enable Astra, and it is off by default at launch.

Astra posts very strong benchmark results. OpenAI reports a 98 percent score on FrontierMath Tier 4, 99.9 percent on ARC-AGI-3, and 100 percent on ExploitBench. The company says Astra has even helped solve long-standing open math problems, while setting new state-of-the-art marks in computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work.

Computer use is a major focus. Astra is trained for professional environments, letting ChatGPT operate a Mac or desktop—including in the background—to carry out multistep workflows and generate polished documents, spreadsheets, and presentations. OpenAI calls it the best software engineering model to date, combining powerful reasoning with reliable action in real applications.

Codex gets a smarter way to manage long sessions. Instead of compacting earlier context into summaries and losing details, Astra can keep notes across context windows and search earlier messages and tool outputs when needed. The experimental feature is optional in Codex now and will become the default for Astra in coming weeks, helping with debugging and large refactors.

Safety and alignment guide the rollout. OpenAI calls Astra 'the most intelligent and aligned model' but notes a 'significant jump in cyber capabilities' that meets the Critical threshold under its Preparedness Framework. That is why early access is limited and why the full release is staggered rather than simultaneous across all plans.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Astra signals that frontier competition is shifting from chat output to reliable, long-running agentic work: controlling computers, managing codebases, and handling cybersecurity. That raises expectations for rivals and may push tougher safety review processes at frontier labs. Developers gain Codex features that reduce context loss in complex refactors and debugging sessions, enabling more independent multi-step coding; however, enterprise controls and additional-credit pricing could limit experimentation. Regular users should expect noticeably stronger automation in ChatGPT over time, but these capabilities arrive slowly and with safeguards due to real dual-use risks. The staggered rollout also reinforces that big releases can be constrained by security concerns and business strategy, not just technical readiness.
report.tools: For hands-on follow-up, keep an eye on OpenAI’s Codex app and ChatGPT desktop app, especially the experimental Astra context-memory feature that’s now rolling out. Developers can also test GPT-6 Astra through the OpenAI API and AWS once available. Useful reference points include OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework and Daybreak cybersecurity program, along with the FrontierMath and ARC-AGI-3 benchmark suites used to evaluate Astra.
